test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which legislation enacted in August 2025 provides a regulatory framework for safe online gaming in India and aims to protect citizens from the threat of online money-gaming activities?

options.text: The Online Gaming (Control and Regulation) Bill, 2025
The Internet Safety and Gaming Bill, 2025
The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025** was introduced and enacted in **August 2025** to address the rapidly evolving digital entertainment landscape in **India**.
 
• The primary objective of this legislation is to establish a comprehensive **regulatory framework** that ensures a safe and transparent environment for **online gaming** while curbing illegal **online money-gaming** activities.
 
• It aims to protect **citizens**, particularly the youth and vulnerable sections, from the adverse effects of gaming addiction and the financial risks associated with unregulated **betting** and **gambling** platforms.
 
• The bill mandates the registration of all **online gaming intermediaries** and requires them to adhere to strict **KYC (Know Your Customer)** norms and **age-gating** mechanisms to prevent minors from accessing age-inappropriate content.
 
• It also provides for the creation of an **Online Gaming Regulatory Authority**, which is tasked with overseeing compliance, resolving disputes, and ensuring that games do not violate the **sovereignty** and **integrity** of **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regulatory Context in India:**

 
 
• Before the **2025 Bill**, **online gaming** was primarily governed through amendments to the **Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021**, issued by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**.
 
• The **2023 amendments** introduced the concept of **permissible online games** and required the formation of **Self-Regulatory Bodies (SRBs)** to verify games.
 
 
 
• **Taxation and Revenue:**
 
 
• The **GST Council** of **India** decided in its **50th meeting** to impose a uniform **28% GST** on the full face value of bets placed in **online gaming**, **casinos**, and **horse racing**.
 
• This move was aimed at bringing parity in taxation and increasing **government revenue** from the high-growth **gaming sector**.
 
 
 
• **Skill vs. Chance:**
 
 
• Indian jurisprudence traditionally distinguishes between **"Games of Skill"** and **"Games of Chance."** While games of skill are protected under **Article 19(1)(g)** of the **Constitution**, games of chance are often categorized as **gambling** and regulated strictly by **State Legislatures**.
 
• The **Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025** seeks to bring a unified **Central law** to provide clarity on these definitions at a national level.
 
 
 
• **Player Protection Measures:**
 
 
• The legislation emphasizes **responsible gaming**, requiring platforms to display warnings about financial risks and time spent, and to provide mechanisms for **self-exclusion** for players showing signs of **addiction**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Impact:** The **Indian online gaming industry** is one of the fastest-growing sectors, with a projected **CAGR** of over **20%**. The **2025 Bill** provides the necessary legal certainty to attract **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**.
 
• **Prohibited Content:** The bill strictly prohibits any **online game** that involves **wagering** on the outcome of real-life events or any activity that resembles **money laundering**, as per the **Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002**.
 
• **Enforcement:** Non-compliance with the provisions of the **Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill, 2025** can lead to heavy **penalties**, blocking of the **gaming platform** under **Section 69A** of the **IT Act**, and criminal proceedings.
